newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks ease off highs, glitch hits trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks ease off highs, glitch hits trade.

text.p: SPI 2583.0 +1.0 US 30yr (Fri) 6.99 steady
10yrbond futs 92.425 +0.045 Gold NY (Fri)342.50 Lon342.55
*Stocks opened slightly lower but trading was temporarily halted by technical problems. Volume 50.12 million, value A$68.71 million, 471 stocks traded, 225 steady, 138 up, 108 down.
Australian stocks eased off their record highs at Tuesday's opening as traders continued to mark down BHP following its profit warning on Monday.
Trading was also affected by technical problems with the stock exchange's trading system, SEATS.
At 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.3 points lower at 2,579.5, with the market having little offshore guidance due to market holidays in New York and London.
The June contract of the share price index was up one point at 2583.0, slightly increasing its discount to the underlying physical market.
Brokers said trading was relatively quiet.
"It's not going to go a great deal one way or the other," said Peter Struk a dealer at Reynolds & Co.
"BHP will have to come off a bit further yet because of the downgrading, so you will probably see a bit of buying coming into Western's and MIM's," Struk said.
Analysts have downgraded their earnings forecasts for BHP following Monday's announcement that it expected a flat performance until it restructured and started new projects.
At 10.55 a.m. (0055 GMT), BHP was 16 cents down at A$18.76.

The fall added to the A$760 million wiped off BHP's market value on Monday, when it fell 40 cents. "With both the big overseas markets closed, we obviously lack in general direction and I expect a pretty quiet day with low volumes and narrow ranges," said Steve Mayne, a dealer at Brisbane broker Nevitts.

Banking and insurance shares paused for breath after strong gains following Friday's surprise cut in cash rates by the Reserve Bank. Shares of retailers and building related companies were also steady after receiving a boost from the rate cut.

FAI Insurances topped the turnover lists again, with over 18 million shares going through the market with most of the trade crossed before the opening. On Monday, about 20 million FAI shares were traded. Brokers said Macquarie Equities have been handling all the recent trades in FAI.
Drug research group Norvet jumped over 33 percent on the announcement that it had achieved patent protection in the United States for a range of its products.
Both the industrial and resource sectors were broadly weaker.

In other market news, Australian bond yields edged lower, but trading remained light in the absence of a guiding light from the U.S. market. At 11.15 a.m. (0115 GMT), the 10-year T-bond was five basis points lower at 7.56 percent.
The Australian dollar was recovered from a US$0.7635 low offshore and looking to squeeze higher with the market still short after Friday's 1-1/2 cent plunge.
At 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT), the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7652/57, compared with Monday's late trade of US$0.7662/67.
